events.what: Bourgain and Demeter bound the number of k-th powers in arithmetic progressions whose step has O(1) divisors
Novaković shows that for progressions with step q ≲ N^r the number of squares among N terms is N^{1/2+ε}

judgement.doubts: The result loses an ε in the exponent (N^{1/2+ε}), so even on its restricted class it does not reach Rudin's conjectured O(√N); it is a bound on a restricted class, not a settled case. The record says the author describes the argument as something that 'should be known', an extension of Bourgain–Demeter, so its novelty is thin; one could also read it as a weaker-form variant, which would leave the problem open. The 2018 Bourgain–Demeter date is taken from the arXiv identifier (month only).

corrections.why: F3/F1: the record's own summary says Theorem 1.4 gives N^{1/2+ε}, 'matching Rudin's conjectured O(√N) exponent up to the ε'. That does not prove the O(√N) bound for the restricted class of progressions, so no case is settled. It is a bound (scope bound → progress), and the record called it a 'claimed-quality single-case result', which mixes up scope and verification. The competing_reading already leans toward progress/bound.
F14: a progress row settles nothing, so it carries no direction.
